analysis.title: Americas Utilities: Power - IPPs: Updating estimates for select IPPs following earnings and elections, prefer PJM over ERCOT in near term
key_insights: The IPP group is down 23% YTD after derating following the Texas elections. GS sees the pullback as a buying opportunity over 12 months and the market as having overreacted relative to likely near-term fundamentals.
GS lowers target multiples across select IPPs to reflect heightened uncertainty but still sees about 44% average total return across coverage.
Ratings: Buy on VST, NRG and TLN, Neutral on CEG. TLN is the relative preference because it has no Texas exposure. CEG is Neutral on relative valuation but seen as more defensive near term.

The Texas election campaign focused on pausing data center development until legislation with guardrails passes. The 2027 legislative session runs January to May, so GS expects more volatility until policy language is introduced.
Texas exposure by company: NRG has about 47% of capacity and 52% of gross margin in Texas, VST about 39% and 40%, CEG about 25% and 18%, and TLN has none.

Hedging limits 2027 earnings risk. GS estimates VST is about 93% hedged on an output-weighted basis and NRG has 75% of expected 2027 ERCOT generation hedged as of October. Risk rises for 2028 and beyond as hedges roll off.

VST expects 2027 realized Texas pricing of $51.34/MWh against a $38.50/MWh ERCOT North ATC forward. Management's path to about $24/share of FCFbG in 2030 assumes no recovery in ERCOT pricing beyond the forward curve.

NRG management says marking both ERCOT and PJM to current curves would still support its 14%+ long-term EPS and FCFbG/share growth target. GS sees more risk to the timing of upside than to near-term earnings growth.

GS's Texas load forecast does not underwrite the whole data center pipeline. The 451 dataset shows Texas data center IT capacity of about 12 GW in 2027 and up to 18 GW by 2030. GS forecasts 1.8 GW average annual demand additions in 2027-2030 and about 2.4 GW in 2029.

ERCOT's interconnection queue is about 474 GW, leaving room for projects to be delayed or dropped while still supporting load growth. NRG says Texas demand is growing above 3% without data centers. TCEQ authorized an air permit for SpaceX, which GS reads as supportive of demand.
Valuation on GS 2027 estimates: NRG about 7x EV/EBITDA, VST about 8x, TLN about 8x, CEG about 12x. The group's 8-year average is about 9.5x EV/EBITDA and about 11% FCF yield.

CEG trades at a 56% premium to the other IPPs on 2027 EV/EBITDA versus a historical premium of 46%. GS says this leaves less upside if new contracts or earnings growth take longer than expected. The FCF yield premium is in line with history.

Buybacks: TLN has a $3 bn program through 2028 including a $1.5 bn ASR. VST has about $2.5 bn left and targets at least $1 bn a year. NRG plans $3 bn across 2026-27. CEG has about $2 bn left. GS sees NRG repurchasing about 10% of market cap annually from 2027.

NRG's proposed ~$4 bn sale of ~4.9 GW across ISO-NE, NYISO and ERCOT would fund $2 bn of debt paydown and $1 bn of buybacks, with $1 bn left for growth or debt reduction. NRG keeps its full PJM portfolio and a large Texas position.

VST's Cogentrix acquisition (closed October 30) adds about 5.5 GW, reduces Texas to just under 40% of generation earnings, and is expected to bring high-single-digit FCF accretion near term and double-digit from 2029.

CEG's Peak+ offering pairs nuclear output with batteries, demand response or new capacity to sign long-term contracts. CEG also plans about 1.2 GW of nuclear uprates, mostly online between 2029 and 2032.

Estimate changes: GS 2027-2029 EBITDA moves for VST to $8,092/$8,621/$9,063 and for NRG to $5,883/$6,345/$6,629. CEG 2026 EPS rises from $12.00 to $12.80. GS 2026/27 EBITDA is about 2% above consensus across coverage.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut from $200 as the EV/EBITDA multiple falls from 10x to 9.25x and the target FCF yield rises from 7% to 7.75%. The Cogentrix close and 93% hedging of 2027 support earnings. The text once cites $183 but the comp sheet shows $184.

Price target cut from $167 as the EV/EBITDA multiple falls from 8.5x to 7.5x and the target FCF yield rises from 9% to 10.5%. It has the most Texas exposure but the deepest valuation discount and the largest buyback relative to market cap.

Price target nudged from $316 to $318 on 3Q results and PPA announcements, with target multiples unchanged. Neutral on relative valuation, with lower Texas exposure making it more defensive near term.
Relative preference in the group because it has no direct Texas exposure. Total return to the target is 41% with an 11.4% 2027 FCF yield.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees the post-election selloff as a 12-month buying opportunity with about 44% average total return. Near-term preference is PJM over ERCOT exposure.

earnings_insights: VST: GS estimate of 2026 EBITDA moves from $7,330 to $7,358 (GS estimate, vs consensus $7,330). GS 2027-2029 EBITDA moves from $7,924/$8,891/$9,151 to $8,092/$8,621/$9,063. Model now includes the Cogentrix acquisition closing October 30 and a PJM West zonal basis discount.

NRG: GS estimate of 2026 EBITDA moves from $5,505 to $5,688 (vs consensus $5,466). GS 2027-2029 EBITDA moves from $5,851/$6,413/$6,800 to $5,883/$6,345/$6,629. Model now reflects new hedging disclosures and company guidance.

CEG: GS estimate of 2026 EPS moves from $12.00 to $12.80 after 3Q results (reported in the quarter, no figures given in this note). GS 2027-2029 EPS moves from $13.23/$17.10/$19.93 to $13.26/$17.03/$19.82. GS 2026 EBITDA is $8,743 vs consensus $8,603.
TLN: GS EBITDA estimates sit above consensus, at $2,200 vs $2,127 for 2026 and $2,850 vs $2,673 for 2027 (GS estimate vs FactSet consensus).
VST management expects 4-6% load growth through 2030 and FCFbG/share growing from about $14 in 2027 to about $24 by 2030. Management guidance, not GS estimates.
NRG's 1.2 GW Texas data center deal is described as an important near-term catalyst.

macro_indicators.indicator: ERCOT North ATC power price forward
macro_indicators.interpretation: Forward curve price is well below VST's $51.34/MWh expected realized price, which is lifted by hedges struck before the curve fell. Shows weaker ERCOT pricing is already priced in for 2027.
Supports the demand case even with near-term data center uncertainty. NRG separately cites Texas demand growing above 3% without data centers.
Large queue leaves room for delays and cancellations while still supporting load growth, per GS.

trade_ideas.description: Buy the IPP pullback over 12 months, with TLN as the relative preference and VST and NRG also Buy rated
trade_ideas.rationale: GS sees the post-election derating as an overreaction relative to near-term fundamentals, with 2027 earnings largely hedged.
trade_ideas.risk: Texas legislative outcome on data center development, lower than anticipated power prices, PJM capacity auction uncertainty.

risk_factors: VST: PJM capacity auction uncertainty, lower than anticipated power prices, and the future of the power demand theme.
NRG: increased headline risk tied to AI and the data center theme, lower than anticipated power prices, PJM capacity auction price uncertainty.
CEG: regulatory and interconnection risk, lower or higher than anticipated power prices, slowdown or acceleration in data center demand.
Texas policy: a pause on data center development until legislation with guardrails passes, with the 2027 session running January to May.
Hedge roll-off: NRG has more power price exposure in 2028 as hedges roll off, with higher risk of project delay from 2028 onward.
PJM regulatory changes could push some data center projects out.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 and 2 show Texas share of company capacity and gross margin: NRG 46.8% and 51.7%, VST 38.8% and 40.1%, CEG 25.2% and 18.0%, TLN 0%.
Exhibit 3 shows 2027 hedge coverage: NRG ERCOT 75.0%, NRG PJM 90.0%, TLN total fleet 70.0%, VST Texas 93.5%, VST East 92.7%, VST West 97.0%.
Exhibit 4 shows VST's 2027 Texas pricing bridge from $38.50/MWh ATC hub plus $12.84 from hedges and premium to $51.34/MWh realized.
Exhibit 5 shows NRG 2027 ERCOT power-price sensitivity from a $46/MWh base, ranging from +$740mm at +$20/MWh to -$570mm at -$15/MWh.
Exhibit 7 shows 451 Research projecting Texas data center IT capacity of 12 GW in 2027, 13 GW in 2028, 16 GW in 2029 and 18 GW in 2030.
Exhibit 12 and 13 compare current EV/EBITDA (VST 7.7x, NRG 7.1x, TLN 8.0x, CEG 11.8x) and FCF yields (VST 9.3%, NRG 14.4%, TLN 11.4%, CEG 5.0%) with 8-year historical averages.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects potential for more volatility in the IPPs into the Texas legislative session (January to May 2027) until policy language is introduced.
The IPP group is down 23% YTD. CEG trades at a 56% premium to peers on 2027 EV/EBITDA versus a 46% historical premium.

tension_points.bull_case: Texas remains a key long-term growth market. VST and NRG are 93% and 75% hedged for 2027, ERCOT's queue of about 474 GW is overstated, NRG sees Texas demand growing above 3% without data centers, and air permits such as SpaceX's are being approved.
tension_points.bear_case: The election campaign focused on a pause on data center development until legislation with guardrails passes, which could slow load growth and weaken ERCOT power price upside. Risk rises in 2028 and beyond as hedges roll off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Policy language introduced during the 2027 Texas legislative session (January to May) that pauses or restricts data center development, or project delays as hedges roll off in 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: CEG has a nuclear PTC floor, a growing long-term contracted book, lower near-term Texas exposure, and new contract routes through Peak+ and about 1.2 GW of uprates.
tension_points.bear_case: CEG trades at a 56% EV/EBITDA premium to peers versus a 46% historical premium, leaving less upside if contracts or earnings growth take longer than expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: New contracts or earnings growth arriving later than expected would undercut the premium multiple.

theme_stances.key_argument: Texas remains a solid long-term demand market even if some load takes longer to come online, and heavy 2027 hedging insulates near-term earnings.
theme_stances.evidence: we have not seen anything that changes the longer-term demand story

theme_stances.key_argument: CEG's premium to peers is wider than its historical premium, leaving less room for upside if contracts or earnings growth are delayed.
theme_stances.evidence: this leaves less room for upside if new contracts or earnings
